title: Extract a Signed Sensor Reading
statement:
Not every field is a flag or a count. A lot of sensor hardware -- an
accelerometer axis, a thermocouple reading, a microphone sample -- hands back
a **signed** two's-complement value packed into fewer bits than an `int`,
sitting inside a register that also carries status flags in the bits around
it. Reading it out is *Extract a Register Field* plus one more step: deciding
where the field's own sign bit is, and extending it correctly.

## Your function

```
int extract_signed_field(unsigned int reg, int start, int width);
```

`start` and `width` mean what they meant in the two register-field problems:
`start` is `0` to `31`, `width` is `1` to `32`, `start + width <= 32` always.
Extract the field, then treat it as a `width`-bit two's-complement number and
return its value sign-extended to a full `int`.

`extract_signed_field(0xFFF, 0, 12)` is `-1`: the low 12 bits are all set,
which is `-1` in 12-bit two's complement, whatever is sitting in bits 12-31.

## Watch out

- **The sign bit is bit `width - 1` of the field, not bit 31 of the
  register.** A register carrying a 12-bit reading typically has other
  things in bits 12-31 -- status flags, a second channel, padding -- and
  none of it is meant to affect the sign of this field. Mask the field down
  to its own `width` bits *before* you test or use its top bit; test on the
  masked field, never on the raw shifted register.
- **`width` can be `32`**, same as the other two register problems, and the
  mask you build from it needs the same special case -- `1u << 32` is
  undefined behaviour.
- A portable way to sign-extend without shifting a signed value at all: if
  the field's top bit is set, subtract `1u << width` from it (computed as
  `sign_bit << 1`, using the sign bit you already found, so the same `width
  == 32` care applies there too). Everything stays unsigned until the final
  cast back to `int`.

tests.name: a -1 reading among status flags
tests.description: Bits 3-14 are all set: -1 in 12-bit two's complement, whatever bits 0-2 and 15 happen to be.

tests.name: a positive reading among status flags
the whole register, width = 32
tests.description: Same width == 32 mask case as the other register problems, this time combined with sign extension.

tests.name: a positive field with the register's own top bit set
tests.description: Bit 31 of the register is 1, but the field is bits 0-7, whose own top bit (bit 7) is 0 -- the field is positive regardless of the rest of the register.

tests.name: a negative field with the register's own top bit clear
tests.description: The mirror image of the case above: bit 31 of the register is 0 this time, but the field is still bits 0-7, whose own top bit (bit 7) is 1 -- the field is negative regardless.
